findings.claim: T133-OMEGA-STATUS: Live status, death, residue, and rebirth are distinct typed predicates and morphism classes.
findings.failure_mode: The promoted claim is wider than the current Lean subset. `proofs/PROOF_LEDGER_1_3_3.md` binds this row only to `declared_death_blocks_live`, and `formal/lean/OC133V12.lean` proves only a live/death contradiction under explicit hypotheses. The proof does not use `residueOf` or `rebirthOf`, proves no residue/rebirth typed-predicate separation, and establishes no morphism-class structure for this theorem. The finite runner likewise checks boolean death/live/cycle fields and `residue_class != identity_class`, but no rebirth separation.
findings.required_repair: Split the claim into the actually proved live/death consistency row, or add Lean definitions and theorems using `residueOf`, `rebirthOf`, and explicit morphism classes with paired finite positive/negative cases for live/death/residue/rebirth separation.

findings.claim: T133-ID: Residue preservation and rebirth are not identity continuation unless declared identity invariants are preserved.
findings.failure_mode: `formal/lean/OC133V12.lean::invariant_lost_blocks_identity` only proves that `restartClass` returns non-identity when `identityInvariant x y = false`; `restartClass` ignores `residueOf` and `rebirthOf`. The current proof therefore does not cover residue preservation, does not require a residue-to-new-live rebirth path, and does not separately classify residue versus rebirth. The finite runner reduces the theorem to string/boolean checks on `morphism`, `identity_invariant_preserved`, and `classified_as_identity`.
findings.required_repair: Formalize residue-preservation and rebirth relations with domains/codomains and identity-invariant preservation conditions, prove residue and rebirth cases separately in Lean, and add finite controls where preserved residue without invariant and rebirth with/without invariant are independently tested.

findings.claim: T133-ID title: Identity, residue, and rebirth morphism classification theorem; comparator wording: typed objects, morphisms, categorical semantics / typed morphism discipline.
findings.failure_mode: The categorical wording is not supported by the Lean subset. `formal/lean/OC133V12.lean` defines only an enum `MorphismClass` and a classifier function; it has no morphism record, source/target typing, identity morphisms, composition, associativity, identity laws, category instance, functoriality, or categorical semantics. Calling this a morphism classification/category result is theorem theater relative to the machine-checked artifact.
findings.required_repair: Either rename the public wording to non-categorical tag/classification language, or add an explicit category/morphism formalization in Lean with source/target, identities, composition, and laws, then bind the theorem inventory and finite checks to those formal objects.

findings.claim: T133-CYCLE: Live status requires an explicit cycle mode or non-vacuous maintenance predicate.
findings.failure_mode: The Lean theorem proves only `eligibleLive R x -> supportWitnessed R x`, but `eligibleLive` is defined to include `supportWitnessed`; it does not constrain raw `R.live x = true`. A model can set `live = true` with no cycle and no maintenance unless it is also classified as `eligibleLive`. The public claim says live status itself requires support, which the current Lean subset does not prove.
findings.required_repair: Change the promoted claim to eligible-live classification requires cycle or maintenance, or strengthen `Realization` with a live-support invariant and prove `R.live x = true -> cycleWitnessed R x / R.maintenance x = true`, with finite controls matching that stronger invariant.

findings.claim: T133-MIN: Within the declared OC verdict class, each promoted tuple component is required by a verdict-changing witness pair.
findings.failure_mode: The proof is tautological rather than a minimality proof for the OC tuple. `formal/lean/OC133V12.lean` defines `componentVerdict` as pass iff `present = true`, and `witnessForComponent` sets keep present/drop absent, so every component changes verdict by construction. The finite runner repeats the same self-confirming pattern by accepting component rows when `keep_present` is true, `drop_present` is false, and `changed_fields` names the component. This does not test the actual OC verdict semantics or independence of carrier, residue, morphisms, boundaries, etc.
findings.required_repair: Replace the toy present/absent verdict with the actual OC verdict classifier over the promoted tuple, and provide one-component countermodels whose verdict changes for semantic reasons. Otherwise demote the claim from global minimality to illustrative component toggles.

findings.claim: T133-KLEVEL: Every adjacent K-level transition K0->K12 has a witness, a reduction-failure criterion, and a lawful demotion criterion.
findings.failure_mode: The Lean proof constructs the same generic `retainedTransitionEvidence` for every `AdjacentK`; it does not encode transition-specific added axes, witness pairs, or reduction criteria. `every_adjacent_transition_has_witness` proves `demotionAllowed = false`, while the only demotion theorem proves `lawfulDemotion w -> witnessRetained = false`; it does not prove a lawful demotion criterion exists for every adjacent transition. The finite runner checks flags such as `witness_retained`, `added_axis_observable`, and `demotion_allowed`, but does not evaluate the textual witness or criterion content.
findings.required_repair: Formalize transition-specific witnesses and reduction/demotion predicates for each adjacent K transition, prove both retained-witness reduction failure and lost-witness lawful demotion cases per transition, and make the finite runner evaluate those structured predicates rather than flags and descriptions.
